description: A one-edit request opens no plan at all. The ledger is slow thinking; a single observable unit of work has nothing to decompose, and a plan opened for it is pure overhead the model then has to maintain.
decisions: The eager-init gate is a pure host-side predicate over task-shape features of the prompt alone -- enumerated items, distinct deliverables, conjunction count, length. It reads no benchmark identity and no config profile. The proposal (section 6) says only 'multi-step work' and 'skipped when the prompt is a question'; this fixture fixes the gate as data-driven and names its constants in one place (yi_runtime::plan::gate).

The gate's verdict is advisory to the loop, never to the model: a false verdict suppresses the forced tool_choice, it does not forbid the plan tool. A model that decides mid-run that it does want a plan calls init like any other op.
With no plan open, every non-init op is refused rather than auto-creating one. Auto-creation would make 'view' a mutation and hide the gate's verdict from the transcript.
prompt: fix the typo in README.md: 'recieve' should be 'receive'
